Fueling During and After Exercise 217

The same athletes who avoid rest after an event also tend to overtrain
while preparing for an event. Many sub-elite athletes train for two or
three hours per day, thinking that such a regimen will help them improve.
However, that sort of training program may hurt, not enhance, perfor-
mance. Research has shown that swimmers performed just as well after
one 90-minute training session per day as they did with two 90-minute
sessions (Costill et al. 1991). Quality training is better than quantity training.
Do not underestimate the power of rest.
